chapters.title: k-way merge over the rows

frames.caption: k-way merge over the rows — O(k log n) time, O(n) extra space. Input: kth_smallest(matrix=[[1, 5, 9], [10, 11, 13], [12, 13, 15]], k=9). Step through to watch the code work on this input.
heap = [(matrix[r][0], r, 0) for r in range(min(k, n))] — r = 0
heap = [(matrix[r][0], r, 0) for r in range(min(k, n))] — r = 1
heap = [(matrix[r][0], r, 0) for r in range(min(k, n))] — r = 2
heap = [(matrix[r][0], r, 0) for r in range(min(k, n))] — heap = [(1, 0, 0), (10, 1, 0), (12, 2, 0)]
value, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap) — r = 0; (1, 0, 0) taken from the front of heap; value = 1; c = 0
value, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap) — r = 1; (10, 1, 0) taken from the front of heap; value = 10; c = 0
heapq.heappush(heap, (matrix[r][c + 1], r, c + 1)) — (11, 1, 1) pushed on the front of heap
value, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap) — (11, 1, 1) taken from the front of heap; value = 11; c = 1
value, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap) — r = 2; (12, 2, 0) taken from the front of heap; value = 12; c = 0
value, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap) — r = 1; (13, 1, 2) taken from the front of heap; value = 13; c = 2
value, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap) — r = 2; (13, 2, 1) popped off the end of heap; c = 1
